papers.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
papers.authors: K. Sysoliatina, Akash Vani
papers.abstract: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $τ\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montréal, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.

papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.authors: Dibya S. Chattopadhyay, Carlos A. Argüelles, Vedran Brdar
papers.abstract: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

papers.abstract: The Euclid space mission is dedicated to probing the nature of dark energy and dark matter, through a comprehensive mapping of the Universe's large-scale structure. Central to these cosmological goals are the spectra produced by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) and reduced by the scientific pipelines of the SIR (Spectral near InfraRed) processing function. Due to the intrinsic complexity of slitless spectroscopic data, scientific observations cannot be self-calibrated by the science pipelines. Consequently, the development of dedicated SIR calibration pipelines, utilising specific pointing sequences and observation fields, is essential. The resulting calibration products are fundamental to ensuring that reduced spectra are characterised within requirements in both wavelength and flux. This paper provides a detailed description of the SIR calibration pipelines responsible for generating the products utilised by the science pipelines for Data Release 1 (DR1). A significant challenge in these calibration tasks arises from the requirement to model the entire focal plane as a unified entity. Such a global modelling approach is critical for maintaining astrometric and spectroscopic continuity across the entire field of view. DR1 provides more than 170 millions validated spectra in both red- and blue-grism modes. The accuracy of the reduced spectra is strictly dependent on the performance of the calibration pipelines. Comprehensive analyses of the calibration products and the resulting science spectra demonstrate that current outputs successfully meet the mission requirements. Nevertheless, specific areas for optimisation have been identified; ongoing development is focused on addressing these critical points to further enhance data quality for future data releases.

papers.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
papers.authors: Jegug Ih, Shubham Kanodia, Nicholas Wogan, Mark Fortune, Natalie H. Allen, Hannah Diamond-Lowe, Mike Greklek-McKeon, Måns Holmberg, Jonathan Brande, Reza Ashtari, Katherine A. Bennett, Jacob Lustig-Yaeger, Megan Weiner Mansfield, Andrea S. J. Lin, Caleb I. Cañas, Te Han, Jessica Libby-Roberts, Suvrath Mahadevan
papers.abstract: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. We present RWDDT MIRI/F1500W observations of LTT 1445 A b and c, the transiting rocky siblings in the nearest such system (6.9 pc), comprising two eclipses of each planet across three visits. We perform three independent reductions and a joint fit that includes all existing JWST data and 220 radial velocities, improving the precision on the planetary radii, masses, and orbital parameters by factors of 1.6-2.3. We measure eclipse depths of $157^{+18}_{-17}$ ppm and $154^{+54}_{-37}$ ppm for planets b and c, corresponding to 15 $μ$m brightness temperatures of $528^{+39}_{-29}$ K and $625^{+109}_{-79}$ K, both consistent with the dark, bare rock limit. For planet b, combining these data with the archival MIRI/LRS spectrum in a Bayesian retrieval limits the CO$_2$ partial pressure to $<0.6$ mbar and the surface pressure to $\lesssim0.1$ bar, while forward models exclude thick aerosol layers that could mimic a bare surface in transmission. We conclude that planet b has no substantial atmosphere. For planet c, a potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave the depth poorly constrained; the data rule out only thick, CO$_2$-bearing atmospheres ($\gtrsim1$ bar with $\geq1\%$ CO$_2$). LTT 1445 A b is the planet closest to the canonical XUV-driven Cosmic Shoreline observed in eclipse so far. Its lack of a substantial atmosphere implies that the Cosmic Shoreline cannot lie much farther toward the airless side than nominally predicted.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.authors: Divij Sharma, Roger de Belsunce, Mikhail M. Ivanov
papers.abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

papers.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
papers.authors: William Lake, Paolo Padoan, Åke Nordlund, Troels Haugbølle
papers.abstract: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

papers.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.authors: Lorenzo Valbusa Dall'Armi, Gabriele Astorino, Riccardo Buscicchio, Angelo Ricciardone, Walter Del Pozzo
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

papers.title: Characterising a population of fast-declining SNe Ia in galaxy cluster cores
papers.authors: A. Eranhalodi, J. Nordin, M. Kowalski, U. Burgaz, F. Fischer, M. Ginolin, Y. -L. Kim, T. E. Müller-Bravo, J. Sollerman, A. Townsend, A. Drake, M. Graham, D. Hale, J. C. Jaimes, R. R. Laher, J. Purdum
papers.abstract: Galaxy cluster cores, characterised by old stellar population and suppressed star-formation are ideal for studying the environmental dependence of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). It is unclear whether the diversity of SNe Ia, parametrised by light curve stretch, stems from distinct explosion mechanisms or varying initial conditions, both closely tied to progenitor age. We analyse the light curve stretch and colour distribution of photometrically identified SNe Ia within the galaxy clusters cores, utilising the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) archival data. Using the AMPEL platform, we filter 89,025 ZTF transients spatially coincident with our galaxy cluster catalogues to identify 4,969 likely SN Ia candidates. We split this sample into three populations: core cluster SNe Ia $r \le 0.5R_{500}$, outer-core cluster SNe Ia $0.5R_{500}< r\le 2R_{500}$, and a reference population of non-cluster SN Ia. We present the largest sample of photometrically identified cluster SNe Ia to date, notably isolating a population of 242 SNe Ia within innermost cluster cores $r \le 0.5R_{500}$. This fast-declining SN Ia population is statistically different from the outer-core cluster and field SN Ia population at $\sim4σ$ level. A marginal statistical preference for a bimodal distribution over a unimodal one $ΔAIC$ of 1.53 and 2.3 for each catalogue, indicate cluster cores almost entirely host fast-declining SNe Ia. Conversely, the colour distribution show no significant environmental variation. By filtering out the prompt SN Ia population, cluster cores provide an environment to directly probe the delayed SN Ia progenitor channel. Our observations support a two-population model where progenitor age drives the light curve stretch diversity. The low-stretch values observed in core cluster SNe Ia suggest sub-Chandrasekhar mass double degenerate systems as their likely progenitors.

papers.title: Estimating distances from parallaxes. VII. Computing the three-dimensional kinegeometric posterior with one-dimensional sampling
papers.authors: Coryn A. L. Bailer-Jones
papers.abstract: When parallaxes are of poor quality, proper motions can improve stellar distance estimates using known constraints on stars' physical velocities. Formally this may be achieved via the kinegeometric posterior, a three-dimensional (3D) posterior in distance and velocity for given measured parallax and 2D proper motion. This posterior is the product of a covariant Gaussian likelihood in the parallax and proper motion with a distance and velocity prior that can be constructed from a Galaxy model. In earlier work, I showed how to infer this posterior for stars in Gaia DR3 by explicitly sampling it with a Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. Here I show that this posterior is equivalent to a 1D posterior in distance combined with a sum of 2D Gaussian distributions in velocity. This 1D+2D representation is both faster and more accurate to sample, thereby making the computation of the kinegeometric posterior for a large set of sources much easier.

papers.title: Peak Performance in Matched Filtering: Fused Correlation and Statistically Controlled Screening on CPUs and GPUs
papers.authors: Alexander H. Nitz, Keisi Kacanja, Collin D. Capano
papers.abstract: Batched matched filtering and cross-correlation over large template banks are a primary computational cost in gravitational-wave astronomy, seismology, and radio transient searches. Standard pipelines pair a general-purpose inverse Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with separate multiplication and peak-finding kernels, writing intermediate spectra and full correlation series to memory for every template. We fuse the conjugate product into the first inverse-transform butterflies and the peak reduction into the last so only candidate peaks leave processor registers, and tile batches in 2D so $K^2$ correlations reuse $2K$ cached spectra. This shifts filtering from a DRAM-bandwidth-bound to an on-chip cache-bandwidth-bound regime. In some situations, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is concentrated toward lower frequencies while higher frequencies dominate the transform length. We develop a hierarchical screening method that exploits this via a sequence of short low-frequency transforms before evaluating the full band, deriving stage thresholds from the spectral power profile and matched-filter noise autocovariance to target a specified false-dismissal probability. We demonstrate these methods in the open-source matchedfilter library across eight CPU architectures and two integrated GPUs (AMD Radeon 8060S via Vulkan and Apple M2 via Metal). On an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 at $N=4096$, fused peak-only filtering is $1.4\times$ faster than a standalone AOCL-FFTW inverse transform on one CPU core and $6.2\times$ faster than rocFFT on its Radeon 8060S GPU ($3.1\times$ over MLX FFT on the M2 GPU). For a fiducial gravitational-wave search ($ρ_\mathrm{th}=5.5$, $10^{-2}$ false-dismissal target), hierarchical screening yields a $26\times$ speedup over AOCL-FFTW on CPU, $21\times$ over rocFFT on the 8060S GPU, and $19\times$ over MLX FFT on the M2 GPU.

papers.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
papers.authors: Marta Molero, Luca Boccioli, Almudena Arcones
papers.abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

papers.title: Shedding light on modified recombination scenarios with Rayleigh scattering of the CMB
papers.authors: Debabrata Adak, Elena Vanetti, R. T. Génova-Santos, Jens Chluba, Carlos Hernández-Monteagudo, J. A. Rubiño-Martín
papers.abstract: Rayleigh scattering (RS) of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons by neutral hydrogen and helium, during and shortly after the last scattering surface, adds a frequency-dependent contribution to the CMB anisotropies that scales approximately as $ν^4$ at leading order. The RS signal is most relevant at $200\,{\rm GHz}\lesssimν\lesssim800\,{\rm GHz}$ and could be detected using future CMB experiments. Because RS acts in a frequency-dependent manner which is sensitive to the ionisation history of the cosmological recombination process, it provides an additional probe of the recombination history. This makes it a natural test of modified recombination scenarios, such as variable electron mass $m_{\rm e}$ or fine-structure constant $α$, which have been proposed to ease the Hubble tension. The correlation between the RS and primary CMB signal, both in temperature and polarisation, further enhances its usefulness for constraining cosmological parameters. Using a multi-frequency Fisher analysis with realistic noise and foregrounds, we forecast parameter constraints and biases for PICO and LiteBIRD + Planck. For PICO, adding RS improves the $Λ$CDM constraints on cosmological parameters by $\lesssim7\%$, but improves the constraints on some parameters ($H_0$, $m_{\rm e}$, $α$, $Ω_{\rm b}h^2$, $Ω_{\rm c}h^2$) by $\simeq31\%$ for some modified scenarios in the recombination history. However, the improvement for LiteBIRD + Planck is limited to less than $2\%$ for most of the parameters. Neglecting RS biases the cosmological parameters by up to $\simeq1σ$ for PICO and below $1σ$ for LiteBIRD + Planck. Therefore RS must be modelled in the analyses of future CMB data.

papers.title: The ultraviolet continuum slopes of galaxies at $\mathbf{z \gtrsim 12}$ selected from ${\mathbf{0.6 \, deg}^2}$ of JWST imaging
papers.authors: C. Bondestam, D. J. McLeod, F. Cullen, R. J. McLure, J. S. Dunlop, S. Antonogiannaki, H. -H. Leung, R. Begley, A. C. Carnall, C. T. Donnan, R. S. Ellis, A. Fontana, N. A. Grogin, I. J. B. Holst, G. D. Illingworth, A. M. Koekemoer, F. -Y. Liu, T. M. Stanton, S. D. Stevenson, E. Taylor
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) continuum slopes $(β)$ of $55$ galaxies at $z\gtrsim 12$, selected from a wide-area ($>0.6$ sq. deg) search across publicly available JWST/NIRCam imaging. Our sample spans the absolute UV magnitude ($M_{\mathrm{UV}}$) range $-21.6 \leq M_{\mathrm{UV}} \leq -17.3$ and we find an inverse variance-weighted mean $\langleβ\rangle = -2.57\pm0.04$ indicating that, on average, the galaxy population is extremely blue at $z\gtrsim 12$. The average $β$ at these redshifts is consistent with the intrinsic stellar plus nebular continuum limit in the absence of UV dust-attenuation. Consistent with earlier JWST works, our analysis suggests that the moderately dust-attenuated galaxies at $z \lesssim 10$ become essentially attenuation-free by $z \simeq 11$. We find no evidence for a $β-M_{\mathrm{UV}}$ relation in our $z\gtrsim 12$ sample, indicating that the attenuation-free interpretation applies across all observed UV magnitudes. By augmenting our sample with previous JWST constraints down to $z=9$, and incorporating $M_{\mathrm{UV}}$-matched HST studies down to $z=4$, we find a smooth evolution in $β(z)$ over a wide range in redshift. The average value of $β$ becomes progressively bluer at $z>4$, with $\mathrm{d}β/\mathrm{d}z \simeq -0.1$. Finally, although we find that the typical galaxy at $z \gtrsim 12$ is consistent with the attenuation-free limit, the scatter in our individual $β$ measurements is consistent with the existence of a small population of dust-reddened galaxies with $β\gtrsim -2$.

papers.title: Crest factor optimization of multi-tone signals generated for low-temperature sensor readout
papers.authors: L. H. Arnaldi
papers.abstract: Microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID) are a growing technology of cryogenic detectors and have a great potential in radio-astronomy and cosmic microwave background (CMB) characterization. A review of the general readout performance requirements for experiments requiring the multiplexing of large arrays (~10.000 pixels) of such cryogenic detectors is presented. The focus is on the crest factor optimization process for proper excitation and readout of these large arrays of detectors. It is shown an algorithm to optimize the phase generation of the carriers to obtain a low crest factor, favoring the dynamic range usage of the electronic chain.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.authors: Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Isabelle S. Goldstein
papers.abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

papers.title: Parallel alignment of radio AGN jets and large cosmic web structures in the direction of the Shapley supercluster
papers.authors: I. Baronchelli, T. Venturi, V. Casasola, P. Merluzzi, C. Burigana, G. Busarello, M. Bonato, O. Smirnov, T. Ronconi, M. Massardi, E. Liuzzo
papers.abstract: Aims. We investigated the potential large-scale alignment of radio active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets in the proximity of the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) area and its correlation with the identified cosmic web structures. Methods. We analyzed 28 radio AGNs divided into two populations with comparable sky coverage north and south of a diffuse X-ray filamentary structure connecting clusters in the SSC core. We measured the average jet position angles (PAs) and combined them with spectroscopic redshifts to assess the persistence of the alignment along the line of sight. Results. We detected a significant large-scale alignment of the radio AGN jets with the foreground X-ray filament (oriented at PA $\sim$ 115$^\circ$ $\pm$ 10$^\circ$). Both the northern (PA $\sim$ 117$^\circ$) and southern (PA $\sim$ 129$^\circ$) groups align with this axis, yielding an overall statistical significance of 4.5 $σ$ (upper and lower bounds: 6.1$σ$, 3.8 $σ$). Although the projected alignment is highly significant, sparse spectroscopic coverage (seven sources spanning 0.048 $\lesssim$ z $\lesssim$ 0.55) suggests that this spatial coherence may extend beyond the SSC (z $\sim$ 0.048), hinting at a line-of-sight correlation across significantly larger cosmic scales. Conclusions. The observed alignment cannot be explained by localized dynamical processes alone. These findings may indicate a persistent influence of the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, or preferred directions of matter collapse, on supermassive black hole spin axes, highlighting a connection between AGN jet morphology and the underlying dark matter distribution. Such alignments represent an important systematic that must be accounted for in precision cosmology with surveys such as Euclid.

papers.title: The 21 cm-Lyman-$α$ forest cross-power spectrum with a minimal effective field theory
papers.authors: G. Autieri, V. Iršič, M. Viel
papers.abstract: Intensity maps of the 21 cm line and the Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest trace the same cosmic volume at $2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$. Their cross-power spectrum is insensitive to foregrounds that do not correlate between the two probes and, together with the Ly$α$ auto-spectrum, separates the mean 21 cm brightness temperature from the neutral hydrogen (HI) bias. Effective field theory models of each tracer exist, but at one loop they carry tens of nuisance parameters. We test whether a minimal effective field theory (mEFT), consisting of the tree-level Kaiser model with leading-order counterterms and stochastic terms, previously validated for the Ly$α$ auto-spectrum, describes the 21 cm auto-, Ly$α$ auto- and cross-power spectra jointly. We use the Sherwood 80 $h^{-1}$Mpc hydrodynamical simulation with HI painted onto halos at $z=2.4$-$4.2$, and reduce sample variance with Zel'dovich control variates. Each spectrum is validated separately and then in a joint fit with shared parameters. With scale cuts $k_{\rm max}=0.5$, $1.2$ and $2.0\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for the 21 cm auto-, cross- and Ly$α$ auto-spectra, the mEFT fits all three spectra at all five redshifts. In the joint fit the mEFT determines the HI bias to 2.0-2.5% and the Ly$α$ density bias to 2.1-2.3%. The scale cuts follow the HI velocity dispersion and the Ly$α$ pressure-smoothing scale. When the brightness temperature is left free, the fits that include the cross-spectrum prefer values 20-30% above the true one, at 1-2$σ$, while the two auto-spectra together do not constrain it. A prior on the HI bias recovers the true value of the brightness temperature.

papers.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
papers.authors: Aditya Kumar Sharma, Alicia Calafat, Rodrigo Tenorio, David Keitel, Alicia M. Sintes
papers.abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

papers.title: Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised gaS (BETIS) III. The impact of eDIG on strong-line abundance determinations in galactic halos
papers.authors: R. González-Díaz, E. Pérez Montero, J. M. Vílchez, F. F. Rosales-Ortega, L. Galbany
papers.abstract: The extraplanar diffuse ionised gas (eDIG) is a key tracer of the feedback processes that connect galactic discs and halos. We present the first study of spatially resolved gas-phase chemical abundances in the eDIG of edge-on galaxies, based on integral field spectroscopy obtained with MUSE. Using a sample of four galaxies from the BETIS sample, we derived maps of the oxygen abundance, 12+log(O/H), the nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio, log(N/O), and the ionisation parameter, log(U), with the HII-CHI-Mistry v5.5 code, and we tested the reliability of this method when different ionisation sources are present. We separated the eDIG into star-formation-dominated and shock-contaminated regimes according to the relative contribution of photoionisation and shocks, and investigated their impact on the derived chemical abundances. We find that HII-CHI-Mistry returns systematically lower O/H and N/O values in shock-contaminated regions, especially for N/O, with typical offsets of ~0.1-0.15 dex relative to star-formation-dominated regions, together with a more homogeneous and lower ionisation state (log(U) ~ -3.1). In contrast, star-formation-dominated regions span a wider range of ionisation parameters (log(U) ~ -3.3 to -2.8) while maintaining approximately solar oxygen abundances. Despite these differences, the abundance offsets are comparable to the sampling step of the HII-CHI-Mistry model grid. The inferred oxygen abundance shows little variation between discs and halos. This is compatible with a scenario in which star formation feedback and galactic fountains efficiently recycle oxygen-rich gas between both components, in agreement with hydrodynamical simulations. In contrast, the N/O ratio shows significant radial and vertical variations, particularly in environments with weaker star formation feedback.

papers.title: AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB
papers.authors: Gabriel Tomassini, Andrea Chiavassa, Bernd Freytag, Eric Lagadec
papers.abstract: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

papers.title: On-the-Fly Gaussian Process Reconstruction of the Galaxy Redshift Distribution for 3$\times$2pt Cosmology
papers.authors: Jip de Buck, Guadalupe Cañas-Herrera, Henk Hoekstra, Angus H. Wright
papers.abstract: The joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing, photometric galaxy clustering, and their cross-correlation, the so-called 3$\times$2pt analysis, is one of the primary probes Stage-IV surveys will use to constrain the dark-energy equation of state. Its accuracy depends critically on the calibration of the underlying photometric redshift distributions, $n(z)$, whose residual uncertainties can bias cosmological inference. However, conventional parametric nuisance models may not adequately capture the full range of plausible $n(z)$ uncertainties. We therefore present a cosmological inference framework that instead reconstructs $n(z)$ on the fly using Gaussian Processes (GPs), replacing per-bin shift-and-width parameterisations by a non-parametric, data-driven model. We validate the method on synthetic Euclid-like 3$\times$2pt data vectors representative of Euclid Data Release 1, sampling GP hyperparameters jointly with cosmological and nuisance parameters to reliably propagate $n(z)$ uncertainties into the posterior distributions. We find that the dependence of the inferred parameters on the adopted $n(z)$ model is markedly stronger in $w_0w_a$CDM than in $Λ$CDM. Opening the dark-energy sector both amplifies the biases induced by a given $n(z)$ treatment and changes which $n(z)$ reconstruction the data prefer, so that a model validated in $Λ$CDM does not automatically remain adequate once $w_0$ and $w_a$ are free. Our results thus indicate that Stage-IV surveys should define $n(z)$ uncertainty marginalisation requirements separately in cosmologies beyond $Λ$CDM to ensure unbiased dark-energy constraints.

papers.title: Starspots on eclipsing giant stars II.: TESS continuous viewing zone giant V521 Dra
papers.authors: A. Haris, B. Seli, K. Oláh, S. Rappaport, J. S. Thomsen, M. Turkki, T. Hackman, M. Tuomi, K. Yakut, A. Casasbuenas, M. A. Díaz, J. H. Terwel, B. N. Hauptmann, R. Gagliano, T. L. Jacobs, M. H. Kristiansen, H. M. Schwengeler, M. Omohundro, I. Terentev, B. Powell, V. Kostov, Zs. Kővári
papers.abstract: Eclipsing binaries are exceptional laboratories for stellar astrophysics. By analysing the modulations in their eclipse light curves, we can probe their surface inhomogeneities. The eclipse-mapping technique enables us to scan starspots in detail, using the transit of a companion star across the surface of a spotted star. When multiple consecutive eclipses are observed, this method may also reveal the evolution of spot properties and provide evidence for stellar differential rotation. We study the magnetic activity of V521 Dra, a tidally locked eclipsing binary with a red giant primary and a main-sequence secondary, both of K spectral class, on a 4.27 d orbit. This is an exceptional system with ~5.3 years of TESS 2 min cadence observations. This offers a unique opportunity to study magnetic activity in uninterrupted blocks over several years with very high photometric precision. We aim to constrain the evolution of the spot pattern of V521 Dra A. We used two methods to study the spot activity of the primary: eclipse mapping and analytic spot modelling. We analysed the stellar properties of the system with a set of methods, including combined modelling of the eclipse light curves, radial velocity data, spectral energy distribution analysis, and forward modelling of the whole orbital light curve. The star shows strong spot-induced modulations both in the eclipse and out-of-eclipse parts of the light curve. We identified 540 spot eclipse signals in 203 primary eclipses. Eclipse mapping reveals the presence of up to four spots. The spot longitudes drift continuously in time, indicating differential rotation. Spots in the eclipse-mapping data show differing angular velocities in their drift, implying a near-surface shear in the convective zone of the primary. Using time series spectroscopy and the spectral energy distribution, we constrained the astrophysical parameters of the binary system.

papers.title: Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability
papers.authors: Rajeev Singh Rathour, Radosław Smolec, Vincent Hocdé, Nicolas Nardetto, Oliwia Ziółkowska, Igor Soszyński, Andrzej Udalski
papers.abstract: The O-C method in classical Cepheids traces both evolutionary and shorter-timescale (non-evolutionary) period changes. In our previous works, we found irregular period changes in $\sim$33% of Magellanic classical Cepheids, but excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability. Here, we establish whether first-overtone Cepheids hosting such variability differ in their period-change behaviour from the general first-overtone population. We analyse 544 Magellanic Cepheids with period ratios $P_{\rm x}/P_{\rm 1O} \sim 0.60-0.65$ or $P_{\rm 1O}/P_{\rm x} \sim 0.68$, using OGLE photometry, and classify and characterise their O-C diagrams following our previous studies. We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the LMC and 144 in the SMC), an incidence rate of $\sim$75.5%, a statistically significant increase over the $\sim$68.1% of our previous single-mode first-overtone sample. The combined first-overtone incidence becomes $\sim$69.7%. This provides the first empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anticorrelates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with jitter roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and a shallower scaling with pulsation period.

papers.title: The astrometric precision of incoherent pulsar timing arrays
papers.authors: Anna C. Tsai, Dylan L. Jow, Ue-Li Pen
papers.abstract: We address the astrometric precision with which a pulsar timing array (PTA) can localize a single astrophysical gravitational-wave source, in the regime where pulsar distances are poorly constrained compared to the gravitational wavelength. Using simple matched-filter, map-making simulations, we calculate the astrometric precision of the intrinsic PTA residual response as a function of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where the SNR is that of the source in the matched-filter map, and find that the median angular error decreases as $\sqrt{\ln 2/3}\,/[\mathrm{SNR}\sqrt{\ln\mathrm{SNR}}]$ over the relevant SNR range, with a pre-factor we derive from first principles. At an SNR of 6, this log term coming from the singular core of the convolution kernel produces an angular error approximately $1.4$ times smaller than for a Gaussian beam. We compare this sky-averaged maximum precision with the precision achieved across the sky by the pulsars of the International Pulsar Timing Array (IPTA) DR2. For a map with SNR of 6, the intrinsic array precision is $3.3^\circ$. For the IPTA configuration at the same SNR, the median precision over the sky is worse due to sparse sampling of the underlying pulsar residual response, approximately $8.9^\circ$; however, for sources in $14\%$ of the sky, the high local pulsar density yields a precision better than $3.3^\circ$.

papers.title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
papers.authors: Íñigo Zubeldia, Boris Bolliet, Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro, Pablo Villanueva-Domingo, Miles Cranmer
papers.abstract: LLM-based peer review is now used at production scale, but its evaluation remains limited. We introduce a benchmark that injects objective, localisable errors of four types (general issues, mathematics, numerics, citations) at three severity levels into real papers and measures each reviewer's detection rate by error type and severity, together with its false-positive rate on clean copies. We also present Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer that verifies citation-backed claims by retrieving the cited papers, mathematics with computer algebra, and numerical claims with executed code. We apply the benchmark to two corpora of 15 recent arXiv preprints each, one in astrophysics and one in machine learning (ML), injecting a total of 357 errors, and evaluate twelve reviewer systems: six single-LLM reviewers, two Claude Code configurations, three publicly available reviewers, and Skepthical. The choice of model has the largest impact on detection rate: given the same prompt, three frontier LLMs differ by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora. Tools and scaffolding help when they contribute what the model cannot supply on its own. In particular, on astrophysics, Claude Code improves on a single Claude call in mathematics and numerics detection, and enforced citation retrieval gives Skepthical the highest citation error detection rate of all systems by a large margin. This citation lead, however, is not observed on ML, where the models appear to know the literature better and Skepthical's citation detection rate is statistically indistinguishable from that of the best single LLM. False-positive rates are below 10% for most systems, but vary with prompt, model, and scaffolding, with mathematics flags the main source of false positives. The evaluation pipeline, the injected errors, and the adjudication logs are released as a benchmark.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The Euclid surveys at DR1
papers.authors: Euclid Collaboration, I. Tereno, J. Dinis, X. Dupac, R. Scaramella, B. Altieri, H. Aussel, I. Baldry, P. Battaglia, G. Buenadicha, C. Burigana, B. Carry, P. Casenove, J. -C. Cuillandre, C. Dominguez-Tagle, A. Franco, B. R. Granett, M. Granvik, A. Gregorio, B. Y. Irureta-Goyena, R. Kohley, K. Kuijken, P. Liebing, E. L. Martin, J. Martin-Fleitas, J. Mendes, L. Miller, A. A. Nucita, R. Nakajima, K. Paterson, V. Pettorino, M. Pontinen, G. D. Racca, E. Romelli, M. Schirmer, M. Schmidt, T. Schrabback, D. Scott, C. Sirignano, R. Tata, T. Trombetti, R. Vavrek, A. Zacchei, M. Zerjal
papers.abstract: Euclid is a surveying mission that is progressively imaging and spectroscopically mapping a wide area of extragalactic sky in visible and near infrared bands. The Euclid mission is, however, not restricted to the Euclid Wide Survey, but it includes data from various other survey components. This paper presents the Data Release 1 (DR1) status of the multiple Euclid surveys and fields, including the Euclid Deep Survey, Euclid Auxiliary Fields, calibration fields, the Euclid Medium-Deep Survey, the Euclid Ecliptic Survey, and the Independent Legacy Scientists' field, in addition to the Euclid Wide Survey. Some of these fields were observed during the initial Performance-Verification phase, others during the Phase-Diversity calibration campaign, and the majority during the subsequent science operations phase. This paper describes the different procedures of survey implementation applied in the various phases of the mission, from the set of requirements, constraints, and limitations, to the final operational products used to operate the spacecraft and execute the science surveys. The resulting main component of the Euclid surveys, the Euclid Wide Survey, covers at DR1 an area of 2100$\,{\rm deg}^2$, in two separate regions, of which 1900$\,{\rm deg}^2$ corresponds to data validated in higher-level processing.

papers.title: Rapid Multiparameter Gravitational-Wave Tests of General Relativity with Neural Posterior Estimation
papers.authors: Hong Su, Tao Yang, He Wang
papers.abstract: Multiparameter gravitational-wave tests of general relativity (GR) are limited by strong correlations among post-Newtonian (PN) phase deformations and the computational cost of Bayesian inference. We present DINGO-TGR, a neural posterior estimation framework that jointly infers binary-source parameters and six PN phase deformations within the TIGER parametrization, using IMRPhenomXPHM waveforms with spin precession and higher-order modes. Importance sampling reweights the neural proposal samples, while principal component analysis (PCA) identifies two well-constrained combinations of PN deformations. We validate the framework using 16 zero-noise GR injections and 12 beyond-GR injections, recovering GR-consistent posteriors in the former and leading-mode shifts consistent with the injected deformations in the latter. For GW150914 and GW250114, our results agree with independent \texttt{bilby-tgr} analyses using \texttt{dynesty}. After training, inference including importance sampling takes approximately 38 minutes and 4.4 hours, respectively, compared with 177 and 238 hours for conventional sampling. GW150914 exhibits a mild offset from GR in the leading PCA mode, whereas GW250114 is consistent with GR. To assess the significance of the GW150914 offset, we analyze 1000 GW150914-like GR injections with independent Gaussian-noise realizations and fixed detector power spectral densities. The resulting empirical upper-tail $p$-value is $11.5\%$, indicating that the observed offset does not reject the adopted GR null model at the 5\% significance level. Our results demonstrate the potential of importance-sampling-corrected neural inference for efficient multiparameter GR tests and large-scale injection-based significance assessments.

papers.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
papers.authors: Akihiro Doi, Yoshiyuki Inoue
papers.abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.

papers.title: ALMA quiet Sun observations compared with a simulated MURaM-ChE chromosphere
papers.authors: Maria Loukitcheva, Sami K. Solanki, Damien Przybylski, Stephen M. White, Robert Cameron
papers.abstract: Aims. We assess the ability of the MURaM-ChE enhanced network simulation to reproduce the chromospheric millimeter brightness observed with ALMA and investigate the properties of the simulated emission. Methods. We analyze synthetic brightness temperatures from the MURaM-ChE model in ALMA Bands 3 (3.2 mm) and 6 (1.3 mm) and compare them with ALMA observations of quiet-Sun, network, and enhanced network regions. We examine the statistical properties of the brightness distributions, their dependence on magnetic field strength, and their variation with wavelength, using results from Bifrost enhanced network snapshots as additional reference cases. Results. The MURaM-ChE model reproduces the range and variability of brightness temperatures observed in enhanced network regions, with particularly close agreement found for the 23 April 2017 data set. The reference Bifrost snapshots produce lower brightness temperatures in both bands, with values below even those measured by ALMA in the quiet Sun. The systematic offset between the models is present in both bands and is likely associated with differences in atmospheric density stratification and the resulting effective formation heights. Both the observations and simulations show an overall increase in brightness temperature with magnetic field strength and wavelength, although significant scatter is present. Conclusions. The results indicate that the MURaM-ChE model provides a physically consistent representation of chromospheric conditions in enhanced network regions and captures key properties of the observed millimeter emission. The comparison highlights the sensitivity of millimeter brightness to atmospheric stratification and magnetic structure and demonstrates the diagnostic potential of ALMA observations for constraining chromospheric models.

papers.title: Modelling redshift-space distortions with tracer-centred split densities
papers.authors: Aritra K. Gon, Yan-Chuan Cai, Mark Neyrinck, Andrew Repp, Ravi K. Sheth, István Szapudi
papers.abstract: Analysing galaxy clustering in split environmental densities has been demonstrated to offer an advantage over standard two-point clustering for extracting cosmological information. A major challenge to realising this potential with the density-split (DS) technique is that the observations are in redshift space. This complicates its modelling, primarily because the density-split centres may not be conserved between real and redshift space. We develop a modelling framework that splits on the tracer-centred density PDF, rather than the volume-weighted density PDF commonly used in previous studies. We derive the linear bias associated with the threshold density in redshift space, enabling us to connect large-scale DS clustering to the density PDF. We find that the threshold density field consists of doughnut-like structures, which we term `Island(s)'. We propose an empirical model, analogous to the halo model framework, that comprises linear, non-linear, and stochastic terms and accurately reproduces the anisotropic redshift-space clustering of tracers in each DS bin. Using this model, we confirm that DS clustering can provide tighter constraints on cosmological parameters than the standard two-point statistic. Furthermore, we show that the gain in cosmological information from DS analyses relative to standard two-point statistics arises primarily from knowledge of the density PDF, which incorporates small-scale perturbation modes below the smoothing scale.

papers.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
papers.authors: Daniel Williams, Michael Williams
papers.abstract: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted. We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained. We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0. Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

papers.title: Stellar-Field-Driven Induction Heating Unlikely To Cause Significant Heating in Giant Exoplanets
papers.authors: Madison Brady, Darryl Z. Seligman, Cassidy Walker
papers.abstract: A planet moving through a changing magnetic field will have a current induced on it by that magnetic field. If the magnetic Reynolds number in the upper atmosphere of this planet is small, the dissipation of this current could result in observable changes to the planet's properties. In this paper, we estimated the total power that would be dissipated in the observed giant exoplanet population if they orbited stars with misaligned magnetic dipoles. We found that, even if all planets orbit stars with extremely misaligned surface magnetic fields, the vast majority of known exoplanets are unlikely to dissipate enough magnetic power to cause observable changes in their surface temperatures. We also extended our calculations to estimate the impact that a low-but-nonzero planetary eccentricity would have on the induced power, and provide a code that implements these calculations. Overall, while it is unlikely that any currently known exoplanets are experiencing a high enough degree of stellar-induced Ohmic heating to be observable, we cannot rule out the possibility that an eccentric, inclined planet on a short-period orbit around a superlatively magnetically active star could have observable magnetic heating. We note that our calculations assume that magnetic diffusion dominates over induction in the upper atmospheres of these planets. However, hot Jupiters with large wind speeds may have high magnetic Reynolds numbers and therefore be in the inductive regime.

papers.title: Magnetic blue large-amplitude pulsators
papers.authors: Andrzej Pigulski, Piotr A. Kołaczek-Szymański, Marta Święch, Piotr Łojko, Kacper J. Kowalski
papers.abstract: With the discovery of blue large-amplitude pulsators (BLAPs), one of the most important questions to be answered was in which evolutionary channel(s) these radially pulsating stars could form. Located in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram between hot subdwarfs and main sequence, BLAPs cannot be the products of single-star evolution. Therefore, virtually all scenarios explaining their origin assume binarity at some stage of evolution. One of these scenarios proposed that some BLAPs may have formed as a result of the merger of two low-mass white dwarfs or a white dwarf and a main-sequence star. The merger scenario may result in the formation of a magnetic field in the merger product, as is postulated for magnetic white dwarfs. Pulsations in a star with a strong magnetic field can manifest themselves in a way known from rapidly oscillating Ap stars, i.e. in the form of evenly spaced multiplets (usually triplets) in the frequency spectrum. This phenomenon can be explained by the oblique pulsator model. We have shown that the three evenly spaced frequency modes discovered in the first BLAP, OGLE-BLAP-001, can be explained in this way. Similar behaviour has also been found in two other BLAPs.

papers.title: Localization of gravitational-wave source behind galaxy clusters by gravitational-wave lensing
papers.authors: Brian H. Y. Cheng, Laura Uronen, Souvik Jana, Samuel Lange, Thomas E. Collett, Otto A. Hannuksela
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened new opportunities to study massive object events like merging binary black holes. When combined with electromagnetic counterparts, accurate localization of gravitational-wave sources could allow us to identify their host galaxies and carry out follow-up studies, such as study the environment of merging black holes and determine the Hubble constant. One of the possible methods for precise localization is strong gravitational-wave lensing. Previous studies have considered strong gravitational-wave lensing with galaxy lenses. However, galaxy clusters have yet to be investigated due to the complexity of their mass structures. Here we take the list of known cluster lenses from the Hubble Frontier Fields, simulate lensing properties of gravitational waves from their reconstructions as they would be observed by the ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. When same model family is used in simulation and localization, we find that the correct lens is identified for around 90\% of the simulated events. We also show that the source positions within the cluster can be pinpointed at sub-arcsecond precision with an estimate on source redshift. When we marginalize over all possible lens models for the clusters, the lens identification and localizations remain valid as long as the correct lens model is contained in the available cluster lens models. However, most localization attempts fail at initialization if the correct cluster model is excluded. These tests establish a proof of concept of localization under idealized conditions, while more work is needed to understand the cluster lens modeling discrepancies and reconstruction bias to validate the approach further.

papers.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
papers.authors: Kailib Ryan Doney, Souvik Jana, Otto A. Hannuksela, Paul Martens
papers.abstract: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). The blasts' signal strength depends on the system's geometry and not on the black hole mass. The signal will go silent and renew twice in a full Lense-Thirring precession period.

papers.title: A parametrized simulation code to simulate the response of ground detector arrays to Extensive Air Showers above 100 TeV
papers.authors: Andrea Chiavassa, Andrea Negro
papers.abstract: Surface arrays detecting the secondary particles of Extensive Air Showers (EAS) are one of the techniques used to detect gamma-rays from high-energy sources. To evaluate the reconstruction performance, gamma/hadron separation, and sensitivity of such experiments, many simulations of gamma rays and protons are required. The usual approach is divided into two steps. First, the CORSIKA software is used to generate EAS at the observation level. Then, a GEANT4-based full simulation code is used to simulate the array response. For very large fill factors, above 30-100 TeV, the computational resources required become too demanding. In this work, the authors present an alternative way to evaluate the performance-related quantities of a simulated array configuration through the parametrization of the detector response. We will present the implementation of such software, the validation checks we performed, and the application of this tool to a representative future ground-based water-Cherenkov detector array.

papers.title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
papers.authors: Anwar El Rhirhayi, Jean-Baptiste Fouvry, Julien Barré
papers.abstract: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.

papers.title: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
papers.authors: Haojia Xia, Hong-Bo Li, Enping Zhou, Ren-Xin Xu
papers.abstract: Rapidly rotating compact ergostars have been proposed as alternative central engines for short gamma-ray bursts. However, competing energy-loss channels, such as gravitational-wave emission driven by non-axisymmetric instabilities, could curtail the power available for relativistic electromagnetic outflows. In this work, we investigate the $w$-mode instability of rapidly rotating strangeon ergostars by solving the coupled spacetime and fluid perturbation equations in the Hilbert gauge using a spectral method, without relying on a slow-rotation approximation. We calculate the complex eigenvalues of the axial-led and polar-led $w$-mode branches originating from the fundamental $l=m=2$ modes of nonrotating stars along the maximum-energy-extraction paths of twelve representative strangeon equations of state. We find that both branches remain damped throughout these paths, despite the presence of ergoregions. We further vary the stellar angular velocity to determine the instability thresholds. In every case with an identified threshold, the angular velocity at the corresponding extraction-path endpoint remains below the critical value, with the largest ratio being $0.926$. Our results indicate that the $w$-mode instabilities examined here do not provide a growing gravitational-wave emission channel along the considered energy-extraction paths, supporting the availability of the previously estimated rotational energy reservoirs for electromagnetic extraction.

papers.title: Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS): the Outflow-Luminosity Scaling Relations in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds
papers.authors: Suinan Zhang, Kei E. I. Tanaka, Yichen Zhang, Takashi Shimonishi, Yu Cheng, Kenji Furuya, Asako Sato
papers.abstract: Understanding massive star formation in low-metallicity environments is crucial for constraining the universality of star formation across cosmic evolution. In this Letter, we present the first systematic survey of massive protostellar outflows in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC, $Z\sim$0.2--0.5 $Z_\odot$), as part of the Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS). MAGOS targets 40 massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) with luminosities of (1--23)$\times 10^4$ $L_\odot$ with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.85 mm at a linear resolution of $\sim$0.1 pc. Using CO (3--2), we identify blue- and red-shifted outflows associated with the primary continuum sources toward 29 targets in the LMC and 10 targets in the SMC. Comparing the outflow mass, momentum, energy, and force versus luminosity scaling relations in MAGOS with those in the Galaxy, we find that the LMC CO outflows have a similar slope in the mass-luminosity relation, suggesting that CO remains an effective tracer of massive protostellar outflows at $Z\sim$0.5 $Z_\odot$. In contrast, despite the large scatter, the SMC CO outflows are deficient at high luminosity and show flatter scaling relations than the LMC and the Galaxy. This is consistent with reduced CO abundances due to enhanced photodissociation at high luminosity and low metallicity ($Z\sim$0.2 $Z_\odot$), although the possibility of intrinsically weak outflow launching cannot be ruled out with the current data.

papers.abstract: The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) contains catalogues of sources covering 1900 deg2, including deep coverage of legacy fields that enable an extensive comparison between Euclid imaging and multiwavelength observations from other instruments. The Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field, observed by Euclid and included in DR1, has been observed with the James Webb Space Telescope, resulting in the COSMOS2025 catalogue. We compare the Euclid DR1 photometry with the multiwavelength COSMOS2025 data to assess the accuracy of the photometric measurements produced by the different methods implemented in the OU-MER pipeline. We use both the Euclid Wide and Deep Surveys, focussing exclusively on extragalactic sources. We use the fluxes of COSMOS2025 to predict the expected fluxes in the Euclid bands via spectral energy distribution fitting, while the redshifts are either spectroscopic, for a sample of brighter sources, or photometric, to include fainter sources. Both the fluxes in the common Hyper Suprime-Cam bands and the SEDs from COSMOS2025 are used to validate the analysis and to characterise any biases or limitations of the method. The predicted fluxes and the OU-MER measurements are in good agreement, especially for bright and isolated sources. Median offsets depend on band, photometric method, survey depth, and redshift sample, most well within 10%, the largest offset seen in the NIR bands for the deep photo-z model-fitting measurements. However, complementary measurements on Gaia stars show an opposite trend, highlighting that photometric validation approaches may suffer from intrinsic uncertainties that prevent a thorough assessment of systematic effects. Among the three methods, template-fitting photometry generally shows the smallest offset from the SED-based predictions in the NISP bands and toward fainter magnitudes, while aperture photometry and model-fitting are comparable in IE.

papers.title: Radiative Transfer Modeling of Multi-Shell Molecular Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 15398-3359
papers.authors: Yushi Ishizuka, Shigehisa Takakuwa, Kazuya Saigo, Jinshi Sai, Shu Ishibashi
papers.abstract: Recent high-angular-resolution observations of protostellar outflows have revealed complex spatial and velocity structures that are difficult to describe with a single shell. We have investigated the primary outflow of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 in the H$_2$CO and CS emission observed with ALMA and identified four shell-like components, which trace the cavity walls of the more extended CO outflows. Non-LTE radiative-transfer calculations of H$_2$CO and synthetic ALMA observations of the three-dimensional model show that a common ellipsoidal geometrical form and Hubble-law-like velocity field can broadly reproduce the channel-map and position--velocity structures of the identified shells when the geometry, spatial configuration, and kinematics of each shell are allowed to vary independently. The kinematic timescales and inclination angles of the inner and outer shells are $\sim$1000 yr ($19^\circ$ and $15^\circ$) and $\sim$750 yr ($5^\circ$ and $8^\circ$), respectively. The momentum injection rate of the outer bipolar pair is approximately 2.2 times that of the inner pair. The inferred $\dot{M}_{\rm wind}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ ratios are $0.7$--$3\%$ and $2$--$7\%$ for the inner and outer shells. The observed shell-to-shell differences suggest episodicity of the mass ejection events, where the strength and direction of the outflow activity may vary over short timescales of order $10^2$--$10^3$ yr.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
papers.authors: H. C. Das, J. B. Wei
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $σ/m_χ\sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $σ/m_χ= 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_χ\simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_χ\simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

papers.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
papers.authors: Joshua D. Lothringer, Jeff A. Valenti, Sarah E. Moran, Rhys Collins, Siddharth Gandhi, Seti Norris, William O. Balmer, Peter Gao, Brayden Roberts, Mark S. Marley, Hannah R. Wakeford, David K. Sing
papers.abstract: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~$μ$m spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5). Our observations include spectral features from H$_2$O, CO, CO$_2$, CH$_4$, Na, and K and cover approximately 98\% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects. We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback. While exoREM provides the best fit of the grid models, no 1D-RCE model provides a satisfactory fit to the data, highlighting the complexity of fitting cloudy L-dwarf spectra. Nonetheless, the temperature and cloud properties can be constrained with the 1D-RCE models, while metallicity, C/O ratio, and surface gravity are not well-measured. Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO$_2$ clouds in both objects. The SiO$_2$ is found to be amorphous in structure for J0624 but crystalline in J2148, highlighting important differences in objects of similar spectral type. We also used a non-Bayesian optimization framework to explore a wider variety of cloud scenarios, finding evidence for the inclusion of iron-rich magnesium silicates (Mg$_{0.5}$Fe$_{0.5}$SiO$_3$, MgFeSiO$_4$) in addition to SiO$_2$ in both objects. These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.

papers.title: Combining TTVs, RVs, and astrometry to characterize distant giant companions of transiting hot Jupiters: Application to WASP-4
papers.authors: J. -V. Harre, Louise D. Nielsen, A. M. S. Smith
papers.abstract: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. These mechanisms can leave different imprints on the orbital architecture, but tidal interactions act to erase these imprints for HJs, leading to orbital circularization, realignment, and potentially orbital decay. The latter can be mimicked by the introduction of light travel-time effects (LTTE) caused by an outer giant companion, as for WASP-4$\,$b. We examine the WASP-4 system using newly obtained ESO$\,$3.6/HARPS radial velocity (RV) observations and archival transit-timing data, leveraging the LTTE. Furthermore, we present a novel approach of analyzing HJ systems in sight of $\textit{Gaia}$'s Data Release 4. We propose combining RV, transit-timing, and astrometry data, making use of the LTTE as a proxy for the orbital motion of a possible outer companion. We combine and fit all currently available data and simulate $\textit{Gaia}$ DR4 and DR5 astrometric measurements of WASP-4 and perform an injection and recovery procedure to estimate their impact on the recovered planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c. The procedure employs a combined model that describes RVs, transit timing variations (TTVs) via the LTTE, and astrometry simultaneously. Analyzing the existing data, we improve the planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c, finding a minimum mass of $9.3\pm1.7\,M_\mathrm{Jup}$ with an orbital period of $10\,600^{+1100}_{-1000}\,$d, or about $29\,$yr. Furthermore, we find that there is no significant orbital decay taking place for WASP-4$\,$b. In simulations of $\textit{Gaia}$ DR5, our three-pronged approach reduces the error bars of WASP-4$\,$c's parameters by about $10\%$, $25\%$, and $33\%$ for its orbital period, time of inferior conjunction, and RV semi-amplitude, respectively.
